title: Monolithic Client Library Resource Pooling
damaged_code:
```rust
let legacy_client = LegacyVendorClient::new(); // internally blocks threads forever
```
pattern: Adopting vendor-provided third-party client libraries that perform their own internal, non-configurable resource or thread pooling.
why_bad: These libraries frequently block client threads forever when connections or resources are exhausted, preventing the parent application from setting timeouts, failing fast, or managing its own thread capacity [178, 179].
detection: Identify third-party libraries interacting with networks or external databases that lack configurable timeout parameters or connection-checkout limits, or wrap call sites in block-forever semantics.
counterexample: None (avoid the library or wrap its executions strictly inside an external worker thread pool that can be discarded).
fix: Avoid using client libraries that do not allow full configuration of timeouts and connection-checkout behaviors. If they must be used, wrap calls in a separate thread pool that the parent application can abort or discard on timeout.
source: Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!*, page 81 / passage [178, 179].
